name: 五子棋英语阅读
source: renju.net / RIF International Rules of Renju

passages.title: Why Black Needs Forbidden Moves
text: Renju looks like a simple game. Two players take turns placing black and white stones on a 15x15 board, and the first player to make an unbroken row of five wins. But a beginner who plays black soon meets a strange rule: some moves are simply not allowed. Why would a game punish a player for making a good move?

The answer is fairness. Long ago, players discovered that a skillful first player could win almost every game of ordinary gomoku. Black moves first, builds a threat, and White can only answer. To balance the game, Japanese masters added restrictions that apply only to Black. Black may not make an overline (six or more stones in a row), a double-four, or a double-three. White has no such limits and may even win with an overline.

These forbidden moves are not minor details. They change the whole way the game is played. A white player can deliberately guide Black toward a point where every natural move breaks one of the rules. Black must then play somewhere else, and White completes a line of five on the next turn. This tactic is called trapping the forbidden points.

So the restrictions do not make Renju less exciting. They make it a real contest. Black still has a strong weapon, the four-three fork, but even that must be earned. The rules turn an easy win for the first player into a game where both sides must think many moves ahead.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the forbidden moves in Renju?
options: To balance the advantage of moving first
questions.why: 第一段提出问题，第二段直接说明是为平衡先手优势而设的规则。

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT forbidden for Black?
questions.why: 第二段列出黑方三种禁手；末段说明四三胜是黑方唯一合法的取胜叉杀。

questions.q: What does "trapping the forbidden points" mean in paragraph 3?
options: Black forces White to break a rule
White leads Black into a position where legal moves are unavailable
Both players pass until the board is full
A referee marks the illegal points on the board
questions.why: 第三段说明白方故意把黑方引到没有合法落点的位置，迫使黑方他投。

questions.q: The word "deliberately" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to ______.
questions.why: deliberately 意为“故意地”，与 on purpose 同义。

passages.title: The Open Four: A Weapon You Cannot Stop
text: If you ask a Renju player what to aim for, the answer is often the same: make an open four. A four is a line of four stones that can become five with one more stone. When both ends of that line are free, it is called an open four, and it is practically a win.

The reason is simple. Suppose Black has four stones in a straight line and both ends are empty. White must block one end immediately. But after White plays there, the other end is still open, and Black completes five. Blocking a half-open four is easy because there is only one point to defend. An open four has two, and a player has only one move.

Because an open four cannot be defended, good players spend the whole game trying to create one. You cannot usually build it directly. You first make an open three, a line of three stones that can become an open four with one move. The opponent must then block the three, often close to the stones. If the three is a fake one, blocked by the board edge or by a white stone, there is no need to worry.

Learning to tell a real open three from a fake one takes practice. It also takes patience: a wise opponent will block every serious threat you build. That is why single-line attacks rarely win against strong players, and why the next lesson is the fork.

questions.q: Why is an open four almost impossible to defend?
options: It can become five in two different places
White is not allowed to block it
It uses the center of the board
questions.why: 第二段说明两端都空，对手只能堵一端，另一端仍可成五。

questions.q: According to the passage, how is an open four usually created?
options: By making an open three first
By placing four stones at random
By waiting for the opponent to pass
questions.why: 第三段第一句：“The open four can be created from the open threes only.”

questions.q: What should a player do about a "fake three"?
options: Treat it as a winning threat
Ignore it because it is not really dangerous
questions.why: 第三段末句说明假三并不危险，无需防守。

questions.q: What does the last sentence suggest about the next part of the text?
questions.why: 末句引出下一段主题 fork（一子双杀）。

passages.title: Forks: Two Threats, One Move
text: A single threat is never enough against a careful opponent. If you build an open three, it is blocked. If you build a four, it is answered. To win, you need a move that creates two threats at the same time. Such a move is called a fork.

Renju players name three kinds of forks. Two fours make a 4x4 fork. A four plus an open three makes a 4x3 fork. Two open threes make a 3x3 fork. In each case the opponent can defend only one line, so the other line remains open and wins on the following move. Diagrams in rule books mark these points with letters, but on the board you have to see them yourself.

Here the rules of Renju matter again. For Black, the 4x4 and 3x3 forks are forbidden moves, and so is an overline. That leaves the 4x3 fork as Black's only legal winning fork. For White, all three kinds are allowed. This is not an accident: the restrictions were designed to offset Black's advantage of the first move.

A fork is not always obvious. A three that looks open may be closed by the edge of the board, in which case the 4x3 is not a winning fork at all. Experienced players also look for the "interesting defense", a move far away from the stones that still stops an open three. Judging which threat is real is a skill that separates strong players from beginners.

questions.q: What is a fork in Renju?
options: A move that creates two threats at once
A stone that is placed by mistake
A rule that forbids Black to move
A way to count the stones
questions.why: 第一段直接定义：一步同时制造两个威胁。

questions.q: Which fork can Black legally use to win?
questions.why: 第三段说明 4x4、3x3 对黑方是禁手，4x3 是唯一合法的取胜叉杀。

questions.q: Why does the passage mention the edge of the board in the last paragraph?
options: It can make a three look open when it is not
It is where the game starts
It gives White an extra move
questions.why: 末段说靠近盘边时“看起来是活三”其实不是，因而 4x3 不成立。

questions.q: What is the best title for this passage?
questions.why: 全文围绕 fork 的种类、规则差异与判断展开。

passages.title: A Game That Crossed Borders
text: Gomoku began in China and traveled to Japan, where it became known as five-in-a-row. About a hundred years ago, Japanese masters were not satisfied with the game. When two strong players met, the first player almost always won. A game with such a sure result was not interesting enough to be a sport.

Their answer was Renju, a word that means "connected pearls" in Japanese. The new game kept the 15x15 board and the aim of five in a row, but it added the forbidden moves for Black. Later, the opening was also regulated: the first three stones form one of a limited number of patterns, and the players then decide who will be Black and who will be White.

Today Renju is played far beyond East Asia. The International Renju Federation, founded in 1988, maintains the rules and ranks players from many countries. World championships bring together players from Europe, Asia and elsewhere. Games are recorded move by move and studied afterwards, much as chess games are studied.

The game also changed as it traveled. Several opening rules are now used in different events, such as the Yamaguchi, Soosorv and Sakata rules. They all try to do the same thing: give both players a fair chance while keeping the rich tactics that made the game popular in the first place.

questions.q: Why were the forbidden moves added to gomoku?
options: Because the board was too small
Because the first player won too often
Because White asked for a new rule
questions.why: 第一段说明先手几乎必胜，因此需要新规则。

questions.q: What does "Renju" mean in Japanese?
questions.why: 第二段首句说明该词日语意为“连串珍珠”。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the International Renju Federation?
options: It was founded in Japan in 1988
It organizes games and keeps player rankings
It only works in East Asia
questions.why: 第三段说明该组织维护规则、给棋手评级并举办世界锦标赛。

questions.q: The opening rules mentioned in the last paragraph are designed to ______.
options: give both sides a fair chance
questions.why: 末段末句直接说明目的：让双方都有公平机会。

passages.title: The Opening Rule: Twenty-Six Patterns
text: In ordinary gomoku, the first player simply puts a stone in the center. In tournament Renju, the beginning of the game is more formal. The purpose of the opening rule is to make the first advantage smaller, so that both players must fight for the result.

Under the international rule, two players are first named tentative Black and tentative White. The tentative Black plays the first three moves in the prescribed shapes: two black stones and one white stone. These three stones choose one of 26 patterns, thirteen direct and thirteen indirect. Then the tentative White decides who will actually play Black and who will play White in the game. This right to change sides is an important part of the rule.

After that, the new White plays a fourth stone anywhere on the board. Black must propose two different points for the fifth stone, and White chooses one of them. Only with the sixth move does the special opening end and normal play begin. Passing is not allowed during the first three moves.

For a beginner, all of this can look complicated. But the logic is clear. Black is given the first move and the attack, while White is given the right to choose the useful side. Other opening rules, such as Swap2 and the Yamaguchi rule, arrange the balance in different ways, but they share the same goal.

questions.q: How many opening patterns are there under the international rule?
questions.why: 第二段说明 13 个直指 + 13 个斜指，共 26 个定式。

questions.q: Who decides which player will be Black after the first three moves?
questions.why: 第二段明确 tentative White 有权决定双方执黑执白。

questions.q: When does the special opening rule end?
options: At the end of the game
questions.why: 第三段说明第六手后特殊开局规则结束。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the last paragraph?
options: Opening rules try to balance the two sides
Swap2 is the only useful rule
questions.why: 末段强调各类开局规则虽有差异，但目的一致：保持平衡。

passages.title: The Clock Is Also an Opponent
text: In a Renju tournament, a game is not decided only by the stones. Each player has a clock, and the time runs only while you are thinking about your own move. When you place a stone, you stop your clock and start your opponent's. If the time ends before the required number of moves has been made, you lose the game.

This makes the clock a second opponent. A player who spends too long on an early position may reach a winning position with only a few seconds left. Under byoyomi, the player then has a fixed short time for each move. Mistakes come quickly: a missed open four, a forgotten forbidden point, or a stone placed on the wrong intersection.

Time pressure also changes the opening. Some players choose a familiar pattern to save thinking time. Others deliberately play a complicated one, hoping that the opponent will use up the clock. Both plans are legal, and both are risky.

The rules are strict about claiming a win. A player who wants to win must stop both clocks at the same time as the winning move. If Black makes five in a row but does not notice, and the game continues, the win may be lost. Even a perfect position is worth nothing if you forget to claim it.

questions.q: What happens when the time on a player’s clock runs out?
questions.why: 第一段末句说明超时判负。

questions.q: According to paragraph 2, what can happen under time pressure?
questions.why: 第二段指出读秒时容易漏看活四或禁点而犯错。

questions.q: Why might a player choose a complicated opening?
options: To make the opponent spend more time thinking
questions.why: 第三段说明有人故意走复杂开局，想让对手耗尽时间。

questions.q: What does the last paragraph warn about?
options: Clocks should be stopped by the referee
Five in a row is not always a win
Beginners should not use a clock
questions.why: 末段强调获胜时必须停钟并宣告，否则可能错失胜局。

passages.title: Training the Renju Mind
text: Strong Renju players do not simply play many games. They study patterns. A pattern is a shape of stones that returns again and again: an open three, a jump four, a forbidden point near the edge. Once a player recognizes such a shape at a glance, thinking becomes much faster and more reliable.

Memory research suggests that recognition grows when information returns at the right moment. If you see a new term once and then never meet it again, it disappears. If you meet it just as you are about to forget it, the memory becomes stronger. This is why many learners use cards with increasing intervals: one day, then two, then four, then eight.

Renju terms are especially suitable for this method. A card can show "straight four" on one side and a short definition on the other. Another card can ask what happens when Black makes an overline. On the front of the card, you must recall the answer before you turn it over; only then do you judge whether you remembered it well.

The same idea works for English. A Chinese speaker learning Renju vocabulary needs both the game concept and the English word. Reading a short article about forbidden moves puts the words into context, and a card later in the day brings them back. Little by little, "open three" stops being a translation and becomes a thought.

questions.q: According to the passage, why do strong players study patterns?
options: To recognize shapes quickly and reliably
To avoid using forbidden moves entirely
questions.why: 第一段说明识别棋形后思考更快更可靠。

questions.q: When does a memory become stronger, according to paragraph 2?
options: When the information is repeated constantly in one day
When it returns just before you forget it
When it is written down once
When it is never used again
questions.why: 第二段说明在快要遗忘时再次接触，记忆会加强。

questions.q: What should a learner do before turning over a card?
questions.why: 第三段明确要求先回忆答案，再翻面判断。

questions.q: What is the writer’s attitude toward combining reading and cards?
questions.why: 末段说明阅读提供语境、卡片帮助复习，态度是肯定的。
